questions.stem: Sketch the surface defined by the equation: x^2 + y^2 - z^2 = 1
questions.solution: The equation represents a hyperboloid of one sheet when k > 0. Sketch the surface accordingly.
questions.explanation: An ellipsoid has positive coefficients for all variables; a paraboloid has only one variable squared on one side; and a hyperboloid of two sheets has k < 0.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A (ellipsoid) because it's the most familiar quadric surface. Remember to check the signs of the coefficients.

questions.stem: Sketch the surface defined by the equation: x^2 + y^2 - z^2 = 0
questions.solution: The equation simplifies to (x^2 + y^2) = z^2, which represents two parallel planes when set equal to zero. Sketch the planes.
questions.explanation: An ellipsoid has positive coefficients for all variables; a hyperboloid requires at least one variable squared on each side; and a paraboloid has only one variable squared.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing B (hyperboloid of one sheet) because it's similar to the previous question. However, setting the equation equal to zero eliminates the hyperbolic behavior.

questions.stem: Sketch the surface defined by the equation: x^2 + y^2 = 4z
questions.solution: The equation represents a vertical paraboloid opening upwards. Sketch the paraboloid.
questions.explanation: An ellipsoid has all variables squared and positive coefficients; a hyperboloid requires at least one variable squared on each side; and a cylinder does not have z as a quadratic term.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing D (cylinder) because it's similar to the previous question. However, the presence of z^2 indicates a paraboloidal shape.

questions.stem: Sketch the surface defined by the equation: x^2 + y^2 = 9 - z^2
questions.solution: The equation represents a sphere with radius 3. Sketch the sphere.
questions.explanation: An ellipsoid has all variables squared and positive coefficients; a hyperboloid requires at least one variable squared on each side; and a paraboloid does not have z^2 as part of the quadratic term.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing C (horizontal paraboloid) because of the form x^2 + y^2, but the presence of z^2 indicates a spherical shape.

questions.stem: Sketch the surface defined by the equation: x^2 - y^2 = z
questions.solution: The equation represents a hyperboloid of two sheets. Sketch the oblique hyperboloid.
questions.explanation: An ellipsoid has all variables squared and positive coefficients; a paraboloid requires only one variable squared; and a hyperboloid of one sheet has z^2 instead of z.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing D (hyperboloid of one sheet) because it's similar to the previous question. However, the lack of z^2 indicates a different type of hyperboloid.

questions.stem: Sketch the surface defined by the equation: x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 4
questions.solution: The equation represents an ellipsoid with radii 2, 2, and 2. Sketch the ellipsoid.
questions.explanation: A hyperboloid requires at least one variable squared on each side; a paraboloid does not have all variables squared; and a cone has only two variables squared.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing D (cone) because of the form x^2 + y^2, but the presence of z^2 indicates an ellipsoidal shape.

questions.stem: Sketch the surface defined by the equation: x^2 - z^2 = 4y
questions.solution: The equation represents a hyperboloid of two sheets. Sketch the oblique hyperboloid.
questions.explanation: An ellipsoid has all variables squared and positive coefficients; a paraboloid requires only one variable squared; and a hyperboloid of one sheet has y^2 instead of y.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing D (hyperboloid of one sheet) because it's similar to the previous question. However, the lack of z^2 indicates a different type of hyperboloid.
